summary: This resolution declares that southern border states have unilateral constitutional authority under Article I Section 10 to repel invasions or imminent dangers from cartels and criminal actors because the federal government failed to protect them or enforce immigration laws from 2021-2024.

scores.thoughts: The resolution references billions spent by border states on services for illegal aliens but does not propose, authorize, or alter any federal or state spending levels. It is a declaratory statement on constitutional authority rather than a fiscal measure.
No provisions address tax rates, credits, deductions, or revenue policy of any kind.
Mentions state spending on healthcare for migrants only as background context; contains no policy prescriptions regarding public versus private healthcare systems.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The resolution's core purpose is to affirm that southern border states face an 'invasion' from cartels and illegal crossers and therefore possess unilateral constitutional authority to exclude such persons. It explicitly criticizes Biden-era policies (catch-and-release, reduced asylum standards, halted wall construction) for increasing illegal immigration. This directly advances a restrictionist, enforcement-oriented view of immigration.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
Invokes the constitutional duty to 'provide for the common defense' but does not alter military budgets, force structure, or defense appropriations.
No environmental, regulatory, or climate provisions appear in the text.
Notes state expenditures on services for migrants but offers no changes to welfare programs, eligibility rules, or benefit levels.
Mentions education costs for migrant children only as factual background; contains no education policy reforms.

Highlights fentanyl and other drug smuggling across the southern border and the resulting epidemic, implicitly supporting stronger border enforcement to curb trafficking. This is secondary to the immigration focus and does not address domestic drug laws or enforcement priorities.
Cites crimes committed by illegal immigrants but does not propose sentencing reforms, policing changes, or criminal justice system alterations.
No provisions concerning tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
No discussion of deficits, debt reduction, or fiscal policy.
No content addressing LGBTQ+ legal protections or related civil rights.
No references to foreign assistance programs.
No election administration, voting access, or voter integrity measures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions.
No labor, union, or employment policy content.
No provisions concerning religious exemptions or anti-discrimination law.
